oracle_provenance: Standard normal-approximation two-sample mean-comparison sample-size formula, standard textbook experimental-design statistics; independently hand-verified before implementation. Not copied from any shared Skill fixture.
scope: Bounded normal-approximation two-sample sample-size calculation from declared effect size, variance, significance and power; not a pilot-validated experimental design.

cases.question: Does the standard 80%-power/95%-confidence sample-size calculation match the well-known textbook result and fit within a generous budget?
With the same effect size but a tight sample budget of 50 per group, is the shortfall flagged rather than silently truncated?
Must a significance level of exactly 1 (undefined for the normal quantile) be rejected rather than silently used?
With a tighter effect size and higher required power (90%), does the required sample size correctly grow rather than shrink, confirming the model's own direction of effect?
